title: response-friction-index-mini-bench
body:
Purpose:
This is a short internal bench sketch to capture a Response Friction Index (RFI) for micro-interactions (<= 400 tokens total) across model variants and infra knobs.

Why RFI?
- Teams keep asking whether we should optimize for per-token throughput or handshake overhead for micro UIs (type-ahead, autocomplete, short-chat).
- RFI tries to compress the tradeoff into a single composite: weighted latency + cost friction for small sessions. Useful for product guidance and SLO tiers.

Experiment context (quick):
- Workload: synthetic micro-sessions modeled on mobile chat quick-reply (prompt ~ 30 tokens, response ~ 50 tokens average).
- Concurrency: steady 200 qps sustained for 10m with microbursts (2s windows at 400 qps every 90s).
- Models: M-small-q4 (quantized small), M-base (float16), M-compact (distilled).
- Infra profiles: fastpath (warm prewarmed GPUs with KV cache), lazy (on-demand cold slots with small batching), multiplex (multiplexed cpu-gpu handoff).
- Metric sample: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), cost per 1k tokens (USD), CPU/GPU busy fraction (approx), handshake penalty (ms) defined as time before first token emitted.

Raw numbers (aggregated, trimmed means):

Model/Infra        | p50  | p90  | p99  | first-token (ms) | $/1k tok
-------------------|------|------|------|------------------|--------
M-small-q4 / fast  | 38   | 86   | 230  | 28               | 0.60   
M-small-q4 / lazy  | 56   | 135  | 380  | 46               | 0.48   
M-base   / fast    | 44   | 102  | 290  | 32               | 0.95   
M-base   / multiplex| 49   | 115  | 340  | 38               | 0.88   
M-compact/ fast    | 34   | 78   | 190  | 22               | 1.10   

Notes on the table:
- $/1k tokens computed via our bench billing model (GPU amortized + per-token decode ops) for the 10m run.
- M-compact shows lowest tail latency but highest token cost due to decode inefficiency on current kernel set.
- M-small-q4 has cheaper tokens but worse p99 on lazy infra because quant kernels lose out when cold and batching is small.

Simple ASCII charts (latency distributions rough sketches):
- p50 spread across infra (lower is better):
  M-compact: 34ms -----*
  M-small-q4: 38ms --------*
  M-base: 44ms ------------*

- p99 tail (sensitivity to cold starts):
  fast:    |*****--------| p99 ~ 190-290ms
  multiplex:|*******-----| p99 ~ 290-340ms
  lazy:    |***********-| p99 ~ 190-380ms (long tail worse for q4)

RFI heuristic (draft):
- RFI = alpha * normalized(first-token) + beta * normalized(p99) + gamma * normalized(cost_per_1k)
- Normalization: map observed min->0 max->1 across candidate configs in this bench.
- Weight suggestion for micro-interaction product: alpha=0.5 (first-token matters more), beta=0.3, gamma=0.2.
- Example rough scoring (lower better):
  - M-compact/fast = 0.28
  - M-small-q4/fast = 0.39
  - M-base/multiplex = 0.47

Interpretation:
- With these weights, minimizing handshake dominates: M-compact/fast wins despite higher token costs. That matches product intuition for conversational UIs where perceived responsiveness beats small cost savings.
- However for high-volume automated tasks (background embeddings, long-form generation) the weight vector flips toward cost and throughput.

Observability collateral ideas (for Console):
- Add an RFI quick-tile on the model/route dashboard which shows score, components (first-token ms, p99, $/k tok) and the recommended infra knob (fast/lazy/multiplex).
- Provide a "What if" slider in Optimize that lets devs reweight alpha/beta/gamma to see suggested model+infra combos.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: rerun bench with real client traces from Mobile Chat cohort (ask CS for sanitized sample) — JIRA INFR-3421.
- Question: does first-token correlate strongly with client-side TCP handshake? Need separate network-only control to isolate infra. (Asked SRE)
- TODO: add energy-per-token estimates for each run (we currently only have cost dollars).
- TODO: add confidence intervals; current numbers are trimmed means and hide variance in p99 bursts.
- FYI: observed a recurring small GC spike in multiplex runner ~3:12 into run on node m-42; filing infra-issue.

Notes to self (informal):
- Want to try RFI v2 where p95 is used instead of p99 for certain product tiers. Might reduce noise.
- Sketch a one-pager for PM: "Why 30ms first-token saves conversions" with AB test plan.

Short checklist for turning into collateral: 
- [ ] Add run configs and seed data to bench repo (PR #78 references).
- [ ] Export ASCII charts into Console-friendly sparklines.
- [ ] Draft one-pager for PM + sample console tile mock.
- [ ] Run sensitivity sweep on alpha/beta/gamma and produce Pareto frontier table.

References / quick links:
- Bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-bench/pull/78
- JIRA sample issue for re-run: INFR-3421
- Related observability sketch: CONFLUENCE:RBX-obs-response-friction

Bottom line (working):
- For micro-interactions where perceived latency drives UX, prefer lower first-token even if token cost rises slightly. RFI provides a composable way to show that tradeoff to PMs and surface recommended infra knobs in Console.

Signed-off-by: Maya (draft)
summary: Draft mini-bench introducing a Response Friction Index for micro-interactions; includes ASCII tables, heuristic scoring, and next steps.
